name: Morva Ube-Rose Praline Coins
description: Small coin-shaped pralines with a synth-dark shell and a whipped ube-rose filling, pressed with a geometric lotus pattern on the face. Sold in lacquered paper boxes of eight.
flavor_profile: Bittersweet synth-dark exterior giving way to sweet purple ube creaminess and a delicate rosewater floral that doesn't overpower
cultural_context: Morva praline coins are the standard gift for formal apologies, condolences, and professional thank-yous in Tier 3-4 culture. The lotus pattern is recognized across social contexts as a signal of intentional, considered gifting. Giving someone a box of Morva means you thought about it — which is itself the message. They're rarely eaten alone and almost always shared with deliberate ceremony.
story_hooks: A box of Morva ube-rose coins arrives at a Tier 4 executive's desk with no sender information on the morning a major internal investigation is announced — and everyone in the office has a theory about what it means.

The lotus pressing dies used for Morva coins are over sixty years old, maintained by a single technician who is the last person who knows how to calibrate them — when she dies suddenly, the 'authentic' Morva coin is in jeopardy.

A Tier 1 forger has gotten hold of Morva's lacquered box design and is selling convincing counterfeits filled with cheap synth-candy, specifically targeting Tier 3 buyers trying to impress Tier 4 contacts.
